requested.title: Headless Chrome is launched with --no-sandbox for every run, not just CI
Sitemap <loc> rebasing fails to pin the origin for non-special schemes, so a <loc> can choose the URL Chrome navigates to
Unvalidated --concurrency makes the link check pass vacuously with exit code 0
rebase() can return a non-http(s) URL, crashing the run with an unhandled rejection instead of skipping the entry
pretty-bytes is permanently excluded from the vendored-version check
Non-directory entry in vendor/ (e.g. .DS_Store) aborts the whole run via unhandled rejection
GitHub repo name is used as the npm package name, discarding the owner

rawResponses.rawText:
I have everything I need. Let me finalize my analysis.

**Verification summary of what I confirmed in the source:**

| Claim | Verified |
|---|---|
| `CHROME_BACKEND` (L136) unconditional, used at L284 + L468 | ✅ — and `bun-types` confirms `argv` = flags appended to the spawned Chrome; docs note Chrome is spawned **once per process**, so the preflight's flags govern every tab |
| Commit `13dc6cb8` "pass --no-sandbox so Chrome launches under Bun.WebView **in CI**" | ✅ intent was CI-only, applied unconditionally |
| `protocol`/`host` setters are no-ops for non-special schemes | ✅ per WHATWG URL spec: scheme state w/ override returns when url's scheme is non-special and buffer is special; host setter returns on opaque path |
| `file:` escalation in F2 | ❌ — `file:///x` has an *empty host* and a *non-opaque path*, so the host setter **does** fire → `file://mochi.fast/x`. No local file read |
| `buildSitemapXml()` is fully static | ✅ `SITE_BASE` hardcoded + static `demos[]` + in-repo doc/post slugs |
| `check-links.ts` L44 unvalidated vs. siblings L79-82 / L52-55 validated | ✅ |
| `Math.min(NaN,n)`→NaN→`Array.from({length:NaN})`→`[]` | ✅ ToLength(NaN)=0 |
| `new URL(rel, 'data:…')` throws | ✅ no-scheme state returns failure when base has an opaque path and `c` ≠ `#` |
| `pretty-bytes` has no `github.com` anywhere | ✅ grepped the whole dir — zero hits |
| `.DS_Store` gitignored (L44), platform darwin | ✅ |
| All 4 parsing vendors: repo name == npm package name | ✅ sindresorhus/debounce, js-cookie/js-cookie, luyilin/json-format-highlight, simov/slugify |
| `check-links` wired into CI | ❌ — only `package.json` L48; no workflow references it |

```json
[
  {
    "findingId": "F1",
    "verdict": "true-positive",
    "adjustedSeverity": "MEDIUM",
    "reasoning": "Confirmed exactly as described. CHROME_BACKEND at L136 hardcodes argv: ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-dev-shm-usage'] with no environment condition, and it is the backend for both the preflight probe (L468) and every per-page WebView (L284). I checked the local bun-types declaration (bun.d.ts ~L9745-9812): argv is 'Extra command-line arguments appended after the default flags' of the spawned Chrome, the defaults are '--remote-debugging-pipe --headless --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check --disable-gpu --user-data-dir=<temp>' (no sandbox flag), and critically 'Chrome is spawned once per process — the first new Bun.WebView() call's path/argv/dataStore.directory win' — so the preflight's flags govern every tab for the whole run. --no-sandbox genuinely disables Chrome's OS-level renderer containment, including under new headless. git log confirms the intent: commit 13dc6cb8 is titled 'fix(site-health): pass --no-sandbox so Chrome launches under Bun.WebView in CI', i.e. a CI-only need implemented unconditionally. The script's purpose is to render and execute remote pages (and it demonstrably loads third-party JS — IGNORE_PATTERNS L103-106 mutes noise from the external u.khromov.se/u.js analytics script), so the weakened boundary is exercised on every run. Two calibrations against the finding's write-up: in CI the blast radius is smaller than claimed — site-health.yml declares 'permissions: contents: read' and the job references no secrets, so there is no meaningfully privileged GITHUB_TOKEN to steal; and the workflow_dispatch 'base' input can only be set by someone who already has repo write. The real residual risk is therefore the local-developer case the finding identifies, and exploitation still requires a Chrome renderer vulnerability, making this hardening/defense-in-depth rather than a directly exploitable flaw. I am keeping MEDIUM only because it is the lowest security tier available in the severity enum; on a Low/Medium/High scale this belongs at Low. The recommendation (gate the flags on process.env.CI) is correct and free, and the same unconditional pattern was introduced by that commit into packages/site/scripts/bake-og-assets.ts and shoot.ts, which are outside this finding's file scope but worth fixing together."
  },
  {
    "findingId": "F2",
    "verdict": "true-positive",
    "adjustedSeverity": "BUG",
    "reasoning": "The URL mechanism is real and I verified it against the WHATWG spec, but the security impact does not hold, so this is a correctness defect, not a MEDIUM vulnerability. Mechanism: for a <loc> like 'data:text/html,<script>…', new URL(loc, base) at L185 ignores the base and yields an opaque-path URL; 'rebased.protocol = origin.protocol' (L190) is a spec-mandated no-op because scheme state with a state override returns when url's scheme is not special and the buffer is special; 'rebased.host = origin.host' (L191) is a no-op because the host setter's step 1 returns when the URL has an opaque path. The value is then added at L192 with no http(s) re-validation (unlike base itself at L88) and handed to Page.navigate at L372. So fetchSitemap() does not uphold the origin-pinning contract its own comment (L181-182) states — that part is confirmed. Why the security claim fails, on three independent legs. (1) Unreachable: I read buildSitemapXml() in packages/site/src/lib/docs.ts — every <loc> is built from the hardcoded SITE_BASE constant plus static demos[] hrefs and in-repo doc/post slugs, so no attacker-influenced bytes can reach a <loc>. (2) No privilege gain even if reachable: the precondition is an attacker who controls the sitemap bytes of the origin the operator chose, and such an attacker can already serve arbitrary HTML+JS at an ordinary https URL of that origin, which this script will navigate to and execute. data: lands in an opaque origin and javascript: executes against the preceding about:blank context (L296) — both strictly *less* privileged than a real origin. (3) The file: escalation the finding hedges on resolves against it: 'file:///etc/passwd' has an empty host and a NON-opaque path, so the host setter's opaque-path guard does not trigger and it is rewritten to 'file://mochi.fast/etc/passwd' — no local file read. The only residual is a non-special scheme without '//' reaching an external protocol handler, which headless Chrome blocks absent a user gesture. I am calling this true-positive rather than false-positive because the defect itself is genuine and the fix is worth applying for contract hygiene (and to avoid the same no-op-setter pattern being reused in product code where origin pinning does carry weight, e.g. the SSRF guard), but the severity must drop to BUG and the security impact should be withdrawn. This keeps F2 consistent with my F4 verdict on the identical mechanism in check-llms.ts."
  },
  {
    "findingId": "F3",
    "verdict": "true-positive",
    "adjustedSeverity": "BUG",
    "reasoning": "Confirmed end-to-end, and the strongest finding in this batch. L39-44 parses --concurrency with a bare Number(next) and parseArgs returns it (L52-56) with no validation — I verified the contrast the finding draws: site-health.ts L79-82 and check-llms.ts L52-55 both reject '!Number.isFinite(concurrency) || concurrency < 1', so this is an inconsistency rather than a deliberate omission. pool() at L68 sizes workers with Array.from({ length: Math.min(limit, items.length) }); Math.min(NaN, n) is NaN and Array.from's array-like path runs LengthOfArrayLike → ToLength(NaN) → 0, so a non-numeric value yields an empty worker array and Promise.all([]) resolves instantly. Math.min(0, n) = 0 and Math.min(-1, n) = -1 → ToLength = 0 give the same result. Both call sites take concurrency directly (crawl at L157, link check at L205), so with `--concurrency abc` (or 0, or -1): no page is fetched, so `links` and `pageErrors` stay empty; `targets` is empty so the second pool does nothing; broken/trailingRedirects stay empty; `failed` is 0 at L252; and L253-255 prints '✓ All 0 links OK across N pages.' and exits 0. Because `pages.length` is non-zero, the success line reads as though real work happened. Two minor corrections to the write-up, neither affecting the verdict: `--concurrency ''` is actually caught — an empty string is falsy, so the `if (!next)` guard at L41 exits 2 — and the script is not in CI (I grepped .github/ and the only reference anywhere is the package.json L48 alias), so the impact is a developer-run check that reports success while verifying nothing, rather than a guaranteed-green CI gate. Both recommended fixes are right; hardening pool() itself is the more durable of the two since all three scripts share that helper."
  },
  {
    "findingId": "F4",
    "verdict": "true-positive",
    "adjustedSeverity": "BUG",
    "reasoning": "Verified, including the throw, which I traced through the URL spec rather than assuming. rebase() (L85-96) assigns u.protocol and u.host; as established in F2 both are spec no-ops for an opaque-path URL, so a non-special-scheme <loc> is returned unchanged and pushed into `pages` at L169 — the 'Skipping unparseable <loc>' branch never fires, exactly as claimed, and the docstring at L84 ('Re-point an absolute URL … at base') is therefore false for that input. Downstream, expectedForPage() L146 evaluates new URL(`${withSlash}llms.txt`, pageUrl) with pageUrl = 'data:text/html,x'. This does throw: the parser finds no valid scheme in the relative input, restarts in no-scheme state, and that state returns failure when base has an opaque path and the first code point is not '#' — so new URL raises a TypeError, which is not caught, and main() is invoked bare at L360 (no .catch()), unlike site-health.ts L515-518 which does wrap it. The result is a raw unhandled rejection instead of a reported finding. On reachability I reached the same conclusion as for F2 — buildSitemapXml() emits only hardcoded-origin https URLs, so the sitemap trigger cannot occur today, and the finding honestly says so. What makes this a true positive rather than a purely hypothetical note is that the second half of its recommendation is independently reachable: L184 does JSON.parse(await fetchText(`${base}/llms.json`)) and fetchText only exits on !res.ok, so a 200 carrying an HTML error body — precisely the failure mode this script checks for at L270-273 — makes JSON.parse throw and kills the run with an unhandled rejection and a raw stack instead of a clean exit 2. That is a plausible dev-server/proxy misconfiguration, not an attacker scenario. So: no security impact (hence BUG, matching the assigned severity), but a verified contract violation plus a verified and reachable missing-error-handler gap, both worth fixing as recommended."
  },
  {
    "findingId": "F5",
    "verdict": "true-positive",
    "adjustedSeverity": "BUG",
    "reasoning": "Confirmed with direct evidence. VENDORED_FROM_RE (L8) requires the literal 'Vendored from https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>…' form. I grepped every vendored index.ts: debounce, js-cookie, json-format-highlight and slugify all carry a conforming github.com line (and json-format-highlight's '/tree/master' variant is absorbed by the regex's optional (?:\\/\\S*)? group, so it matches correctly), while packages/mochi/src/vendor/pretty-bytes/index.ts L1 reads '// Vendored from `pretty-bytes@7.1.0` (MIT, Sindre Sorhus). Trimmed: no BigInt'. A separate grep for 'github.com' across the entire pretty-bytes directory returned zero hits, so the regex cannot match anywhere in the file. Execution therefore takes the `{ name, error: 'no \"Vendored from\" comment found' }` branch at L17-19 and `continue`s at L26-29, and fetch to registry.npmjs.org is never reached — so 1 of the 5 vendored packages is never compared against upstream, which is the script's entire purpose. The compounding exit-status claim also checks out: the missing-comment branch and the npm-lookup-failure branch (L33-36) both only log and continue, there is no process.exitCode or process.exit anywhere in the file, and main() is called bare at L45, so `bun run check-vendored-versions` exits 0 even having checked nothing. The documented workflow amplifies it: .claude/skills/update-vendored/SKILL.md Step 1 says the script 'prints, per vendored script: the pinned version … and the latest version on npm. If everything is current, report that and stop.' One calibration: the failure is not fully silent — the pretty-bytes row is printed in red with the error text — so an attentive operator would see something is wrong; 'never actually compared to upstream, with a success exit code' is the accurate statement rather than 'invisible'. Both recommended fixes are appropriate; normalizing the header is the minimal one, and the exit-code hardening is what prevents recurrence."
  },
  {
    "findingId": "F6",
    "verdict": "true-positive",
    "adjustedSeverity": "BUG",
    "reasoning": "Confirmed, and distinct from F5 — different line range and a different root cause (directory enumeration vs. provenance parsing), so not a duplicate. L11 calls readdirSync(VENDOR_DIR) without { withFileTypes: true }, so `dirs` contains every entry including plain files, and L15 unconditionally awaits Bun.file(`${VENDOR_DIR}/${name}/index.ts`).text(). For a file entry the resulting path has a non-directory parent, so the read rejects (ENOTDIR/ENOENT). Because every read is inside Promise.all at L13 and main() is invoked with no .catch() at L45, the first rejection discards the whole batch: not one package is reported, including the four with valid provenance comments, and Bun surfaces it as an unhandled rejection with a raw stack rather than an actionable message. I verified the trigger is mundane rather than contrived: .DS_Store is listed at .gitignore L44, and this session's platform is darwin, so any Finder visit to packages/mochi/src/vendor/ creates one while `git status` stays clean — the script would simply start failing with no cause visible in version control (I confirmed `git status --short` is currently clean apart from an unrelated .deepsec/ directory, so no such file exists right now; this is latent, not currently firing). The same crash occurs for any future vendored package laid out across multiple files without an index.ts. The inconsistency the finding highlights is real and is the clearest argument for the fix: the script already degrades gracefully for a missing provenance comment (per-package error row) but hard-fails the entire run for a missing file. All three recommended changes — withFileTypes filtering, a per-entry try/catch producing an error row, and main().catch() — are correct."
  },
  {
    "findingId": "F7",
    "verdict": "false-positive",
    "reasoning": "The code reading is accurate but it describes no defect that manifests, and the security framing does not apply. L20's `const [, , repo, pinnedVersion] = match` does skip match[1] (the owner) and take match[2] as `repo`, which L21 assigns to npmPackage and L32 interpolates into https://registry.npmjs.org/${npmPackage}/latest — so the owner is indeed discarded. But I checked every provenance string in the repo and all four that parse map the repo name to the correct npm package 1:1: sindresorhus/debounce → debounce, js-cookie/js-cookie → js-cookie, luyilin/json-format-highlight → json-format-highlight, simov/slugify → slugify. Every current lookup therefore resolves to the right package, and the fifth vendor (pretty-bytes) never reaches this code at all for the independent reason established in F5. More importantly, the typosquat/wrong-package framing requires an input the attacker does not control: the GitHub path is a string we author in our own first-party source file, so an attacker would need commit access to packages/mochi/src/vendor/*/index.ts — at which point they would simply edit the vendored code directly rather than redirect a version-reporting fetch. There is no untrusted data flow here. The scoped-package sub-claim is also purely hypothetical: no scoped vendor exists, and the finding itself concedes this is 'a latent correctness issue rather than an active one.' Two further mitigations limit even the hypothetical: the lookup only prints a version string (it does not download or install anything), and SKILL.md Step 2.1 independently anchors the package name to the vendor folder name ('Note the npm package name (matches the vendor folder name so far in this repo)'), so the replace-wholesale step in Step 3 is driven by the folder name, not by this regex capture. The recommendation — record the npm name explicitly and cross-check the fetched manifest's `name` field — is sensible defensive hardening and would be worth doing alongside the F5 fix, but there is no present-day incorrect behavior and no attacker path, so this does not stand as a BUG finding."
  }
]
```
